question: A fixed-dose combination of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole (co-trimoxazole) is a rational FDC because both components act on the same target via sequential steps in the folate synthesis pathway, producing synergistic bactericidal activity.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Reconsider. Co-trimoxazole is indeed rational: trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase — sequential enzymes in folate synthesis. This sequential blockade is the pharmacological basis for synergy and the defining feature of a rational FDC.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Co-trimoxazole is a textbook example of a rational FDC: both drugs inhibit the same metabolic pathway (folate synthesis) at sequential steps, producing additive-to-synergistic bactericidal activity. It satisfies the criteria for rational combination — complementary mechanism, proven efficacy advantage, and fixed-ratio clinical validation.
